message.content: Lion (Panthera leo) and zebra (Equus quagga) are both placental mammals, but they belong to different orders—Carnivora for the lion and Perissodactyla for the zebra. Their most recent common ancestor is the ancestor of the clade **Laurasiatheria**, which includes all modern placental mammals that evolved on the northern supercontinent Laurasia. This ancestor lived roughly 90–100 million years ago, long before the diversification of the specific families that give rise to lions and zebras today.
